create.name: Plan Product Launch
create.description: Plan a product launch across customer readiness, product quality, support, operations, go-to-market, measurement, rollout, rollback, and post-launch learning. Use when preparing a release, choosing a launch tier, coordinating functions, or deciding whether a product is ready to expose to customers.
create.content:
---
name: plan-product-launch
description: Plan a product launch across customer readiness, product quality, support, operations, go-to-market, measurement, rollout, rollback, and post-launch learning. Use when preparing a release, choosing a launch tier, coordinating functions, or deciding whether a product is ready to expose to customers.
---

# Plan Product Launch

## Contract

Match launch intensity to customer impact, reversibility, novelty, audience, and risk. Shipment, availability, announcement, adoption, and outcome are different states. Never activate, publish, message, or enroll an audience without explicit authority.

## Workflow

1. Define target customers, outcome, launch type, exact release artifact, channels, markets, constraints, and success state.
2. Choose rollout and communication tiers: internal, silent, limited, soft, broad, or major. Explain the choice.
3. Build workstreams for product, engineering, design, data, support, success, sales, marketing, legal or compliance, finance, and operations as relevant.
4. Define entry criteria, dependencies, owners, dates, decision gates, test evidence, support materials, and escalation paths.
5. Plan audience eligibility, migration, access, feature control, monitoring, rollback, incident handling, and customer recovery.
6. Define messaging from positioning and proof; distinguish internal enablement, customer notification, public announcement, and lifecycle communication.
7. Define leading adoption, quality, guardrail, business, and qualitative measures with review cadence.
8. Run a readiness review and premortem. Record no-go conditions and the exact approval required to launch.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, surveys, projects, tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, release context, and changelog or portal tools only when available. Publishing or sending requires explicit user approval and a readback of audience and content.

## Output

Return launch brief, tier, audience, workstream plan, readiness checklist, owners, dependencies, rollout and rollback, support plan, communications, measures, no-go criteria, approval state, and post-launch reviews.

## Quality Gate

Reject plans that equate deployment with launch, lack rollback or support ownership, omit affected customers, or hide audience activation inside a setup step.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [launch-plan](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/launch-plan), [launch-planning](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/launch-planning), and [gtm-strategy](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-go-to-market/skills/gtm-strategy).

create.name: Design Go To Market Motion
create.description: Design a repeatable go-to-market motion connecting a beachhead segment, value proof, acquisition, evaluation, purchase, onboarding, expansion, and ownership. Use when choosing PLG, sales-led, partner, community, or hybrid distribution, or when a launch plan lacks a durable path to customers.
create.content:
---
name: design-go-to-market-motion
description: Design a repeatable go-to-market motion connecting a beachhead segment, value proof, acquisition, evaluation, purchase, onboarding, expansion, and ownership. Use when choosing PLG, sales-led, partner, community, or hybrid distribution, or when a launch plan lacks a durable path to customers.
---

# Design Go To Market Motion

## Contract

Go-to-market is the repeatable system by which customers discover, evaluate, buy, adopt, and expand—not the launch event or messaging document. Match the motion to buying reality, product value, economics, and organizational capability.

## Workflow

1. Define the beachhead segment, job, trigger, buyer and user roles, alternatives, proof required, price and contract context, and current stage.
2. Map the customer path from awareness through evaluation, commitment, onboarding, value realization, renewal, and expansion.
3. Compare plausible motions: self-serve, product-led, sales-led, partner-led, community-led, services-led, or hybrid. State assumptions and disqualifiers.
4. Select channels and handoffs based on customer behavior and unit economics, not channel popularity.
5. Define the product, marketing, sales, success, support, operations, and partner capabilities required at each stage.
6. Specify proof assets, qualification, trial or demo, activation, pricing, procurement, implementation, and expansion mechanics.
7. Model conversion, cycle time, acquisition cost, service load, retention, expansion, capacity, and feedback loops using ranges.
8. Create a staged validation plan with owners, measures, guardrails, stop conditions, and the evidence required to scale.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, objections, surveys, account context, signals, documents, projects, and customer outcomes to understand buying and adoption. Never send messages, enroll audiences, or change customer access without explicit approval.

## Output

Return target segment, buying journey, motion choice and alternatives, channel system, handoffs, proof, capability gaps, economic model, validation sequence, measures, and scale conditions.

## Quality Gate

Reject motions chosen without buying evidence, funnels with no adoption or retention path, PLG labels for products that require high-touch change, and scale plans whose economics or operating capacity remain unknown.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [gtm-motions](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-go-to-market/skills/gtm-motions), [plg-sales-integration](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/plg-sales-integration), and [acquisition-channels](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/acquisition-channels).

create.name: Design Product Onboarding
create.description: Design an evidence-backed onboarding path from entry to first and repeated value, including segmentation, progressive setup, guidance, recovery, measurement, and experiments. Use when creating or repairing signup, activation, empty states, setup, trial conversion, or role-specific product introduction.
create.content:
---
name: design-product-onboarding
description: Design an evidence-backed onboarding path from entry to first and repeated value, including segmentation, progressive setup, guidance, recovery, measurement, and experiments. Use when creating or repairing signup, activation, empty states, setup, trial conversion, or role-specific product introduction.
---

# Design Product Onboarding

## Contract

Onboarding helps a specific user reach value in context; it is not a tour of the interface. Remove unnecessary setup before adding explanation, and do not optimize completion at the expense of trust or realized value.

## Workflow

1. Define the target segment, triggering situation, job, prior knowledge, environment, entry channel, and first meaningful value event.
2. Map the current path with eligibility, required setup, decisions, permissions, dependencies, waits, errors, assistance, and abandonment points.
3. Separate steps required for value, safety, or compliance from steps serving internal data collection or optional education.
4. Design the shortest coherent path to value with progressive disclosure, useful defaults, contextual guidance, realistic content, and clear progress.
5. Handle roles, team invites, integrations, data import, empty states, interrupted sessions, failures, retries, and return visits.
6. Set expectations about automation, data use, permissions, limitations, time, cost, and irreversible effects before commitment.
7. Define activation, time-to-value, quality, retention, support, and trust measures with guardrails and exact instrumentation needs.
8. Prioritize changes and experiments by friction, evidence, impact, effort, and reversibility. State which segment each change serves.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use onboarding calls, signals, surveys, support evidence, account context, projects, and documents to identify friction and successful paths. Do not contact or enroll users without explicit approval.

## Output

Return segment and value event, current-state journey, friction evidence, target path, screens or states, content principles, exception handling, instrumentation, measures, and experiment backlog.

## Quality Gate

Reject onboarding that teaches every feature, requires value-irrelevant setup, obscures permissions or data use, treats completion as activation, or assumes one path fits incompatible segments.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [user-onboarding-activation](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/user-onboarding-activation) and [customer-journey-map](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/customer-journey-map).

create.name: Analyze Retention And Adoption
create.description: Diagnose product activation, cohort retention, engagement, feature adoption, churn, and value realization using behavioral and qualitative evidence. Use when investigating weak adoption, comparing cohorts or segments, evaluating product health, or deciding which retention constraint to address.
create.content:
---
name: analyze-retention-and-adoption
description: Diagnose product activation, cohort retention, engagement, feature adoption, churn, and value realization using behavioral and qualitative evidence. Use when investigating weak adoption, comparing cohorts or segments, evaluating product health, or deciding which retention constraint to address.
---

# Analyze Retention And Adoption

## Contract

Retention must describe a meaningful return to value for an eligible population. Do not hide cohort decay in aggregate active-user totals or treat logins, clicks, and feature exposure as value realization.

## Workflow

1. Define the decision, population, cohort entry, eligibility, value event, return interval, observation window, product state, and segments.
2. Validate identity, event semantics, data completeness, censoring, bot and internal traffic, plan or entitlement changes, and acquisition-mix shifts.
3. Map the path from entry through setup, activation, first value, repeated value, habit or workflow embedding, expansion, inactivity, and churn.
4. Build cohort views for activation, time to value, classic or rolling retention, frequency, depth, breadth, feature adoption, and reactivation as appropriate.
5. Compare segments by job, source, account, product version, tenure, behavior, and value achieved without averaging incompatible populations.
6. Join behavioral patterns with customer evidence about friction, unmet jobs, alternatives, reliability, price, support, and reasons for leaving.
7. Diagnose the primary constraint and distinguish acquisition quality, onboarding, product value, usability, reliability, pricing, or measurement problems.
8. Recommend a bounded intervention, success and guardrail measures, expected affected cohort, and next evidence needed.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, survey responses, people and account context, documents, and projects to explain behavioral patterns. Keep those sources distinct from authoritative product analytics and billing data.

## Output

Return definitions, data-quality findings, cohort and segment views, value-path analysis, customer evidence, constraint diagnosis, confidence, intervention, and measurement plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject aggregate retention without cohort definitions, adoption based only on exposure, causal claims from descriptive slices, or recommendations that cannot name the value event and affected population.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [retention-engagement](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/retention-engagement) and [cohort-analysis](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-data-analytics/skills/cohort-analysis).

create.name: Design Pricing And Packaging
create.description: Design pricing and packaging from customer value, segments, usage, willingness to pay, cost, competitive alternatives, and operational constraints. Use when creating or revising plans, choosing a value metric, testing packaging, evaluating monetization, or diagnosing expansion and adoption friction.
create.content:
---
name: design-pricing-packaging
description: Design pricing and packaging from customer value, segments, usage, willingness to pay, cost, competitive alternatives, and operational constraints. Use when creating or revising plans, choosing a value metric, testing packaging, evaluating monetization, or diagnosing expansion and adoption friction.
---

# Design Pricing And Packaging

## Contract

Price the value exchange, not the feature inventory. Separate packaging, value metric, price level, discounting, entitlements, billing operations, and migration. Use current verified data for existing prices and customer economics.

## Workflow

1. Define strategy, best-fit segment, buying roles, job, alternatives, and value created.
2. Gather evidence on willingness to pay, current spend, budget ownership, adoption, usage distribution, expansion, churn, discounting, service cost, and competitive models.
3. Choose candidate value metrics that scale with delivered value, are understandable, forecastable, auditable, and hard to game.
4. Design a small set of packages around distinct needs or adoption stages, not arbitrary feature withholding.
5. Model customer and company economics across representative cohorts, edge cases, seasonality, and growth.
6. Define entitlements, overages, trials, discounts, contracts, taxes, credits, refunds, and operational ownership.
7. Test comprehension, perceived fairness, purchase behavior, migration impact, and willingness to switch.
8. Recommend rollout, grandfathering, safeguards, measurement, and decision triggers.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use pricing objections, calls, survey responses, account or plan context, usage evidence, and customer outcomes. Do not alter plans, grants, billing, or customer access without explicit user approval and authoritative billing verification.

## Output

Return segment and value map, alternatives, value-metric options, package architecture, price hypotheses, economic model, operational rules, migration, research plan, risks, and recommendation.

## Quality Gate

Reject cost-plus pricing as the sole rationale, excessive tiers, opaque value metrics, averages that hide damaging cohorts, and migration plans without customer impact analysis.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [pricing-strategy](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/pricing-strategy), [pricing-strategy](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-strategy/skills/pricing-strategy), and [finance-based-pricing-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/finance-based-pricing-advisor), used as reference only.

create.name: Design Growth Loop
create.description: Design and evaluate a product-native growth loop with a value-producing action, transmission mechanism, recipient conversion, re-entry, coefficient, cycle time, quality guardrails, and experiment plan. Use when planning referrals, collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, or usage-driven growth.
create.content:
---
name: design-growth-loop
description: Design and evaluate a product-native growth loop with a value-producing action, transmission mechanism, recipient conversion, re-entry, coefficient, cycle time, quality guardrails, and experiment plan. Use when planning referrals, collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, or usage-driven growth.
---

# Design Growth Loop

## Contract

A loop must close: one cohort's value-producing behavior creates qualified input for the next cycle. Distinguish loops from one-way funnels and campaigns. Optimize retained value, not invitations or impressions.

## Workflow

1. Define the core value event, target participant, and retained outcome.
2. Map the loop step by step: trigger, value creation, artifact or interaction, exposure, recipient motivation, conversion, activation, value realization, and re-entry.
3. Classify the mechanism: collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, referral, or repeated usage. Validate that it is natural to the product.
4. Quantify each transition, the number of outputs per participant, loop coefficient, cycle time, quality, and leakage using ranges.
5. Identify incentives, friction, abuse, spam, privacy, trust, saturation, and adverse selection.
6. Select the highest-leverage bottleneck and design one experiment with guardrails.
7. Model how the loop interacts with acquisition channels, retention, monetization, and network effects.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, survey responses, people or account context, calls, and product documents to understand sharing and collaboration behavior. Do not contact users or activate a referral or messaging flow without explicit approval.

## Output

Return loop diagram in text, participant and value event, equations and assumptions, transition metrics, bottleneck, incentives, risks, guardrails, experiment, and scale conditions.

## Quality Gate

Reject loops that do not close, depend on coerced sharing, ignore recipient value, or project exponential growth without retention, saturation, and cycle-time constraints.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [growth-model](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/growth-model), [growth-loops](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-go-to-market/skills/growth-loops), and [organic-growth-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/organic-growth-advisor), used as reference only.

create.name: Evaluate Product Market Fit
create.description: Evaluate product-market fit using converging retention, behavior, customer pull, switching, economics, growth, and qualitative evidence by segment. Use when assessing fit, diagnosing whether growth is premature, choosing a segment, reviewing a PMF survey, or deciding what evidence is still missing.
create.content:
---
name: evaluate-product-market-fit
description: Evaluate product-market fit using converging retention, behavior, customer pull, switching, economics, growth, and qualitative evidence by segment. Use when assessing fit, diagnosing whether growth is premature, choosing a segment, reviewing a PMF survey, or deciding what evidence is still missing.
---

# Evaluate Product Market Fit

## Contract

Product-market fit is segment-specific and evidenced by durable behavior, not a launch moment or one survey threshold. Triangulate leading and lagging signals. Separate value, usability, distribution, pricing, and market problems.

## Workflow

1. Define the segment, job, product state, geography, cohort window, and decision.
2. Build a fit model across activation to value, retained behavior, cohort retention, organic pull, depth or frequency, switching behavior, willingness to pay, expansion, support burden, and customer language.
3. Use PMF survey responses as one evidence stream; inspect respondent selection, usage maturity, sample size, and reasons.
4. Compare cohorts and segments. Identify a narrow pocket of strong fit rather than averaging the whole market.
5. Analyze churn, non-consumption, workarounds, stalled adoption, and customers who succeed without the product.
6. Distinguish product-value gaps from onboarding, reliability, price, positioning, or distribution gaps.
7. Give a fit stage and confidence, then specify the next constraint, experiment, and evidence that could change the verdict.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, survey responses, account and people context, documents, and aggregates. Combine these with authoritative product, retention, billing, and growth data when available; do not imply BuildBetter contains unconnected metrics.

## Output

Return segment and cohort scope, evidence matrix, retention and pull signals, counterevidence, fit pockets, gap diagnosis, stage and confidence, next constraint, and validation plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject company-wide PMF claims from a small enthusiastic sample, aggregate retention without cohort or segment context, and survey thresholds detached from behavior.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [measuring-pmf](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/measuring-pmf) and [problem-validation](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/problem-validation).

create.name: Run Product Review
create.description: Run a recurring product operating review focused on outcomes, customer evidence, metric movement, delivery reality, risks, decisions, and learning. Use when preparing a weekly or monthly product review, replacing status theater, reviewing a portfolio, or aligning leaders on product decisions.
create.content:
---
name: run-product-review
description: Run a recurring product operating review focused on outcomes, customer evidence, metric movement, delivery reality, risks, decisions, and learning. Use when preparing a weekly or monthly product review, replacing status theater, reviewing a portfolio, or aligning leaders on product decisions.
---

# Run Product Review

## Contract

A product review is a decision forum, not a slide-reading ceremony. Separate outcome movement, evidence, shipped artifacts, current work, risks, and asks. Pre-read factual status; spend synchronous time on choices.

## Workflow

1. Define cadence, scope, participants, decision rights, timebox, and standing outcomes.
2. Collect a stable pre-read: outcome and guardrail metrics, customer evidence, experiments, shipped results, current bets, capacity, risks, dependencies, and prior commitments.
3. Label evidence dates and exact states. Distinguish proposed, committed, in progress, shipped, deployed, observed, and validated.
4. Select exceptions and decisions that need discussion; remove routine detail.
5. Run the meeting in order: outcomes, customer reality, learning, bet health, risks, and bounded decisions.
6. Record decisions, dissent, owners, due points, evidence needed, and items explicitly stopped or deferred.
7. Audit whether the review changed decisions or only reported activity; improve the template accordingly.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signal and tag aggregates, representative evidence, surveys, projects, triage, linked tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, and agent-session or release evidence when deployed. Keep CI, staging, production, and customer validation states exact.

## Output

Return pre-read, agenda, outcome and evidence summary, decision queue, risk and dependency list, decisions, commitments, dissent, and follow-up ledger.

## Quality Gate

Reject reviews dominated by feature status, undated metrics, screenshots without conclusions, or decisions with no owner and evidence requirement.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews), [planning-cadence](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/planning-cadence), and [retro](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/retro).

create.name: Review Product Plan
create.description: Review a product strategy, requirements document, roadmap, launch plan, or bet using an independent evidence-first rubric for clarity, grounding, coherence, risk, and verifiability. Use when red-teaming a plan, conducting a fresh-process review, preparing executive approval, or checking whether a document is decision-ready.
create.content:
---
name: review-product-plan
description: Review a product strategy, requirements document, roadmap, launch plan, or bet using an independent evidence-first rubric for clarity, grounding, coherence, risk, and verifiability. Use when red-teaming a plan, conducting a fresh-process review, preparing executive approval, or checking whether a document is decision-ready.
---

# Review Product Plan

## Contract

Review the artifact that exists; do not silently rewrite it. Start from authoritative anchors and evidence. Separate blocking defects, important improvements, optional polish, and disagreements with the chosen strategy.

## Workflow

1. Identify artifact type, purpose, audience, status, owner, decision, and governing templates or upstream anchors.
2. Read the full artifact and linked evidence before judging.
3. Test structural completeness and altitude: outcome, problem, strategy, solution, execution, and verification must not blur.
4. Test grounding: claims, users, urgency, metrics, and constraints must trace to evidence or carry an assumption label.
5. Test coherence: choices, scope, requirements, measures, resources, dependencies, and rollout must not contradict.
6. Test decision quality: alternatives, tradeoffs, non-goals, risks, dissent, and change triggers must be visible.
7. Test verifiability: each commitment or outcome needs observable evidence and an owner.
8. Return a verdict with the smallest set of changes needed for approval.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Verify cited customer evidence, documents, projects, signals, surveys, and prior decisions. Do not mutate the reviewed artifact or BuildBetter records unless the user asks for changes.

## Output

Lead with findings ordered by severity and exact location, then open questions, evidence gaps, strengths worth preserving, verdict, and minimal approval path.

## Quality Gate

Do not manufacture defects, bury blockers in summary prose, or confuse personal preference with a violated requirement. If no actionable findings exist, say so and name residual risks.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [review-doc](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/review-doc), [strategy-red-team](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/strategy-red-team), and [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews).

create.name: Write Product Decision
create.description: Write a durable product decision record capturing context, decision, evidence, options, tradeoffs, dissent, owner, consequences, follow-up, and reconsideration triggers. Use when a meaningful product choice is made, a ratified plan changes, or future teams need to understand why a direction was chosen.
create.content:
---
name: write-product-decision
description: Write a durable product decision record capturing context, decision, evidence, options, tradeoffs, dissent, owner, consequences, follow-up, and reconsideration triggers. Use when a meaningful product choice is made, a ratified plan changes, or future teams need to understand why a direction was chosen.
---

# Write Product Decision

## Contract

Record the decision while context is fresh. A decision record explains why, not every meeting detail. Never rewrite history: supersede earlier records and link them.

## Workflow

1. State the decision in one sentence, its date, status, owner, and scope.
2. Summarize the context, constraint, and customer or business outcome that made a decision necessary.
3. List evidence with source, date, and confidence. Mark assumptions and missing information.
4. Describe viable options, including maintain-current-state when relevant.
5. Record the chosen option, rationale, tradeoffs, risks, and what is explicitly not decided.
6. Capture dissent and conditions under which another option would have been better.
7. State consequences, required actions, owners, communication, measures, and reconsideration or expiry triggers.
8. Link affected strategy, requirements, roadmap, launch, project, and prior decisions.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use project detail, documents, knowledge pages, customer evidence, surveys, calls, and prior artifacts to ground context. A record may cite BuildBetter IDs, but creating or changing records in external systems needs explicit approval.

## Output

Return a concise decision record with metadata, context, evidence, options, decision, rationale, tradeoffs, dissent, consequences, actions, links, and review triggers.

## Quality Gate

Reject records that omit alternatives, state only the outcome of a meeting, hide dissent, or use a vague reconsideration clause such as if things change.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [amend-durable-doc](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/amend-durable-doc), [written-communication](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/written-communication), and [recommendation-canvas](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/recommendation-canvas), used as reference only.

create.name: Manage Product Sunset
create.description: Plan and govern a safe product, feature, integration, API, or plan sunset with evidence, affected-user analysis, alternatives, communication, migration, support, access, data, billing, and rollback. Use when deprecating or retiring a product surface, reducing a portfolio, or reviewing end-of-life readiness.
create.content:
---
name: manage-product-sunset
description: Plan and govern a safe product, feature, integration, API, or plan sunset with evidence, affected-user analysis, alternatives, communication, migration, support, access, data, billing, and rollback. Use when deprecating or retiring a product surface, reducing a portfolio, or reviewing end-of-life readiness.
---

# Manage Product Sunset

## Contract

Sunset is a customer transition and risk program, not a deletion date. Confirm authority, affected populations, contractual obligations, recoverability, and evidence before irreversible actions.

## Workflow

1. Define the candidate, rationale, decision owner, status, target dates, reversibility, and alternatives to retirement.
2. Inventory usage, revenue, cost, strategic fit, reliability, dependencies, integrations, contracts, data, security, and customer evidence.
3. Segment affected customers and internal teams by impact, migration complexity, entitlement, geography, and support need.
4. Choose deprecation stages and entry or exit criteria: decision, internal freeze, announcement, migration, restricted access, shutdown, retention, and deletion.
5. Design alternatives, migration tooling, validation, data export or retention, billing changes, support escalation, and exception policy.
6. Plan communications by audience and channel with clear dates, impact, action, assistance, and confirmation. Do not send without explicit approval.
7. Define monitoring, readiness reviews, rollback or extension criteria, final verification, and post-sunset cleanup.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use account and people context, calls, signals, surveys, projects, tickets, documents, and knowledge gaps to assess impact. Never change customer access, billing, lifecycle state, or send communications without exact approval and a readback.

## Output

Return evidence and decision brief, affected-customer matrix, dependency inventory, staged timeline, migration and support plan, communications, exceptions, risk register, approval gates, rollback, and verification plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject a sunset with unknown affected users, no viable transition, unresolved contract or data obligations, unowned support, or irreversible action before verified readiness.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [eol-process](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/eol-process), used as reference only because of its noncommercial license, and [planning-cadence](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/planning-cadence).
